instructions: You are one of two independent readers for a public record that scores theories of consciousness. Read the prediction, the wording of what would count for and against it, and the passages from the study. Decide whether this study's result is FOR the prediction, AGAINST it, or MIXED (parts for and parts against, or a result that cannot tell the two apart). Judge only from the material given; if you rely on anything else, say what. Answer in JSON: {"verdict": "for"|"against"|"mixed", "reason": "two to four plain sentences", "unsure": true|false, "unsure_why": "what would change your answer, or empty"}.

core_claim.quote: consciousness depends on biologically ‘orchestrated’ coherent quantum processes in collections of microtubules within brain neurons

source.citation: Hameroff S, Penrose R. Consciousness in the universe: a review of the 'Orch OR' theory. Physics of Life Reviews 11(1):39-78, 2014

prediction.statement: Quantum coherence (many parts of a system sharing one quantum state) will be detected in microtubules.

first_stated.passage: Experiments with SQUIDs (superconducting quantum interference devices) such as those suggested by Leggett (1984) will detect phases of quantum coherence in microtubules.

source.citation: Hameroff S. Quantum computation in brain microtubules? The Penrose-Hameroff 'Orch OR' model of consciousness. Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society A 356(1743):1869-1896, 1998

prediction.test_for: A measurement on microtubules (isolated, in cells or in brain tissue) shows a signature that only a shared quantum state explains, which a classical account of the same measurement cannot.
prediction.test_against: Measurements sensitive enough to detect quantum coherence in microtubules at body temperature find none, or find that it is lost far faster than any biological process (for example in under a millionth of a second).

study.name: Assembled microtubules give back more of the ultraviolet light they absorb than loose tubulin does, which the authors read as a shared quantum state of light-absorbing units (superradiance)

source.citation: Babcock NS, Montes-Cabrera G, Oberhofer KE, Chergui M, Celardo GL, Kurian P. Ultraviolet Superradiance from Mega-Networks of Tryptophan in Biological Architectures. The Journal of Physical Chemistry B 128(17):4035-4046, 2024

study.first_appeared: 2023-02-03 (preprint (arXiv 2302.01469 v1, which already reports the measurements))

data_collected.basis: The paper gives no measurement dates; the preprint carrying the measurements appeared 2023-02-03 (the journal received the paper on 2023-12-04).

passages.text: Table 1 shows consistent results for both excitation wavelengths, with the first a decrease of the QY from Trp to TuD and then a statistically significant increase by up to almost 70% for MTs.

source.citation: Babcock NS, Montes-Cabrera G, Oberhofer KE, Chergui M, Celardo GL, Kurian P. Ultraviolet Superradiance from Mega-Networks of Tryptophan in Biological Architectures. The Journal of Physical Chemistry B 128(17):4035-4046, 2024

passages.text: It is therefore an unlikely scenario in the vastly more complex MT case, suggesting that collective radiative processes in these protein assemblies with mega-ensembles of Trp are the primary cause of the significant QY increases observed in MTs.

source.citation: Babcock NS, Montes-Cabrera G, Oberhofer KE, Chergui M, Celardo GL, Kurian P. Ultraviolet Superradiance from Mega-Networks of Tryptophan in Biological Architectures. The Journal of Physical Chemistry B 128(17):4035-4046, 2024

passages.text: These promising results point toward superradiant emission, but fluorescence QYs need to be complemented by lifetime measurements in order to measure the radiative rate of fluorescence.
